decisions.decision: Select M2 for the RTX5090 0.8M seed-0 baseline.
decisions.evidence: M2 real-data peak reserved 2836 MiB at 11.61 it/s; full-model loss/output/gradient equivalence passed; eager evaluation avoids a persistent compiled eval graph.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: M1 is slower; M3 saves more memory but is slower and not required for 0.8M; M0 retains the known compiled-evaluation pool risk.

decisions.decision: Prioritize training speed: stop and preserve F0 after four epochs, then start a fresh seed0 run with M4.
decisions.evidence: M4 was the fastest short FP32 candidate, passed full-model loss/output/gradient equivalence, and a real epoch-4 EMA checkpoint inferred eagerly at batch1 with only 610 MiB reserved.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Do not resume F0 because its checkpoint does not archive all RNG streams; do not enable TF32/BF16 or change batch/T because those alter the numerical/training protocol.

decisions.decision: Keep the epoch-53 EMA checkpoint as the primary 5090 baseline; keep epoch-120 EMA as the fixed endpoint and do not substitute the independent P2-best epoch.
decisions.evidence: 120/120 completed with six loadable checkpoint artifacts and no runtime errors. Strict eager re-evaluation gives epoch53 EMA 39.8452/33.2322 and epoch120 EMA 40.9894/33.3666.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Do not call the raw epoch-53 checkpoint the best model; it re-evaluates to 41.6185/34.2645. Do not claim multi-seed stability from seed0.
